title: The Broken Current
premise: August Yarrow, a disgraced mountain guide drowning in debt, is hired by a desperate mining consortium to find a government survey team that vanished in the Serrano Range, leaving intact gear and no tracks. What August finds instead is the team's leader alive, guarding evidence that the concession's mineral survey was falsified — and that the consortium knew. As permits expire in eleven days, August must lead the broken team out through a storm-wracked pass while deciding whether loyalty to the people paying them matters more than the truth they're carrying. In the end, August gets everyone home alive but releases the falsified data publicly, sacrificing their last chance at redemption within the industry — and discovering that belonging was never something to be granted back.
about_author: R. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade outfitting high-altitude surveys before turning to fiction. They write from a small town at the edge of the ranges they can no longer climb.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: August Yarrow, blacklisted and broke, is summoned by the Halvard Consortium to find a vanished government survey team in the Serrano Range. The money clears their debt; the contract's silence clause raises old instincts. POV: August. Emotional beat: wary hope tangled with shame.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: At the abandoned basecamp, August finds tents pitched, food cached, radios functional — and no tracks leading anywhere. A junior guide on the crew, Petra Ilic, quietly notes the compasses all point wrong. POV: August. Emotional beat: creeping unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: The Silence Clause
chapters.summary: A Consortium liaison, Merrick Voss, arrives by helicopter with new instructions: find the team, recover their instruments, tell no one what the instruments contain. August signs anyway. POV: August. Emotional beat: self-contempt dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Into the White Corridor
chapters.summary: The search party pushes up the Serrano drainage through deteriorating weather. Petra proves herself on a sketchy river crossing; veteran climber Desh Okonkwo questions why the survey route makes no sense for geology. POV: August. Emotional beat: camaraderie forming against doubt.

chapters.title: What the Compass Wants
chapters.summary: Petra's altered compass leads them off-route to a hidden cairn marked with survey tape. Inside: a field journal, half-burned, naming falsified core samples. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery souring into dread.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed
chapters.summary: They find Dr. Elena Vasquez, the survey leader, alive in a snow cave, injured and half-starved, guarding a sealed sample case. She refuses to say where her team went. POV: August. Emotional beat: relief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Voss radios: the concession permits expire in eleven days; bring the case or lose everything. Vasquez warns August the samples prove the ore body is worthless — the whole play was a stock fraud. POV: Vasquez. Emotional beat: cornered conviction.

chapters.title: The Missing Five
chapters.summary: Vasquez finally admits she sent her team ahead down the east ridge before the storm; two are unaccounted for. Desh argues they detour to search; August calculates the storm window and says no. POV: Desh. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking against arithmetic.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Ridge
chapters.summary: They find one missing surveyor dead in a crevasse fall — and evidence someone else reached him first, taking his radio. Someone is on the mountain ahead of them. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Voss Ascending
chapters.summary: Voss appears at their camp with two 'contractors,' claiming he's come to help carry the case out. His story about how he found them doesn't hold. POV: August. Emotional beat: the mask slipping, trust gone.

chapters.title: Night Negotiation
chapters.summary: August privately offers Vasquez a deal: cooperate, get down alive, decide about the truth later. Vasquez counters — the case stays sealed until they're past the last checkpoint. Desh overhears everything. POV: August. Emotional beat: bargains made in bad faith, guilt accruing.

chapters.title: The Pass Closes
chapters.summary: A katabatic storm seals the southern pass. The only way out is the east ridge — toward the second missing surveyor and whoever took his radio. Voss insists on pushing south anyway, alone if necessary. POV: Desh. Emotional beat: dread of the necessary choice.

chapters.title: Split Party
chapters.summary: August splits the group: Voss and one contractor take the low route; August, Vasquez, Petra, and Desh climb east. It feels like strategy; it may be abandonment. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the loneliness of command.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: On the east ridge they find the second surveyor alive, sheltering with a stolen radio — he's been broadcasting the fraud to anyone listening, which is how Voss found the mountain. POV: August. Emotional beat: vindication arriving too late to feel like victory.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Voss's contractor intercepts them at a rappel station; a fight on an exposed ledge leaves Desh badly injured catching Petra's fall. The sample case cracks open — worthless rock, exactly as Vasquez said. POV: Desh. Emotional beat: sacrifice without certainty it bought anything.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Carrying Desh, the party crawls toward the extraction point as Voss radios threats: bring the case and the data, or no helicopter comes for any of them. August must choose who to betray. POV: August. Emotional beat: the corrupting weight of power over other people's survival.

chapters.title: False Summit
chapters.summary: August agrees to Voss's terms over the radio — then quietly gives Vasquez the burned journal pages and the real core log, trusting her to carry the truth even if August doesn't survive the handoff. POV: Vasquez. Emotional beat: faith extended without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Broken Current
chapters.summary: At the glacial river crossing, August springs the trap: reroutes Voss onto unstable ice using the faulty compasses, buying the others a crossing while the current takes the sample case downstream. POV: August. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the first honest decision in years.

chapters.title: Extraction Point
chapters.summary: The helicopter comes anyway — Voss, soaked and furious, needs survivors more than silence. But Vasquez has already transmitted the full dataset to a journalist from the ridge relay. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph shadowed by consequence.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: Downvalley, the story breaks: the concession collapses, the Consortium's executives scatter, and Voss is arrested at the airstrip. August expects nothing and receives a formal inquiry notice instead. POV: August. Emotional beat: hollow justice, bracing for the fall.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: August testifies, telling the whole truth including their own signed silence clause — burning the last bridge back into professional guiding. Desh recovers; Petra asks to work with August again someday. POV: August. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: New Bearings
chapters.summary: Months later, August guides a small conservation survey under a nonprofit flag, Petra at their side, a repaired compass on the dash pointing true north. Belonging, August realizes, was built, not granted. POV: August. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
